title: Phosphate and productivity in pond water

plot.label: Line graph of the change in dissolved oxygen over 24 hours in clear bottles of pond water with different amounts of phosphate added, invented pilot data
plot.yLabel: Change in dissolved oxygen in 24 h (mg/L)

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: A class wants to know how phosphate from lawn fertilizer affects the productivity of algae in a pond. They fill clear bottles with pond water, add different amounts of phosphate, and measure dissolved oxygen at the start and after 24 hours in sunlight. A pilot test gave the results in the graph. Identify the independent variable.

rubric.point: The amount of phosphate added to each bottle

parts.sample: The independent variable is the amount of phosphate added to each bottle (0, 0.05, 0.10 or 0.20 mg/L).

parts.label: b

rubric.point: The change in dissolved oxygen in each bottle over 24 hours (a measure of net productivity)

parts.sample: The dependent variable is the change in dissolved oxygen in each bottle over 24 hours, which measures the net productivity of the algae.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write a testable hypothesis for this investigation.

rubric.point: A statement with a direction linking phosphate to productivity or oxygen (not a question, not "affects")
accept: If more phosphate is added, then the oxygen produced will increase
More phosphate will increase algae productivity

parts.sample: If more phosphate is added to the pond water, then the dissolved oxygen produced in 24 hours will increase, because phosphate is often the limiting nutrient for algae in fresh water.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Identify the control group, and describe its purpose.

rubric.point: The bottles of pond water with no phosphate added
Its purpose: a baseline to compare with, showing how much oxygen the algae produce without added phosphate, so any difference can be linked to phosphate

parts.sample: The control group is the bottles with no phosphate added. They are a baseline: they show how much oxygen the algae produce with only the phosphate already in the pond water, so the class can tell whether the extra phosphate caused the larger increases.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Identify one variable that should be held constant, and explain why.

rubric.point: A valid constant: light, temperature, volume of water, source of pond water, starting algae, time, bottle type
accept: the same amount of sunlight for every bottle

rubric.point: Why: that factor also changes photosynthesis or oxygen, so it must not differ between bottles or it could explain the results
accept: temperature changes how much oxygen water holds

parts.sample: The amount of light each bottle receives should be the same, because light powers photosynthesis; if some bottles got more light, they would produce more oxygen for reasons that have nothing to do with phosphate.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: The class also puts one bottle of each kind in the dark for 24 hours. Explain why the dissolved oxygen in the dark bottles decreases.

rubric.point: With no light there is no photosynthesis, but the algae (and other organisms) still carry out cellular respiration, which uses oxygen
accept: respiration uses oxygen and no photosynthesis replaces it

parts.sample: In the dark the algae cannot photosynthesize, so no oxygen is added, but the algae and bacteria in the water keep carrying out cellular respiration, which uses up dissolved oxygen.

parts.label: g
parts.prompt: The pilot graph levels off between 0.10 and 0.20 mg/L of phosphate. Describe what this pattern suggests, and explain one possible reason.

rubric.point: Adding more phosphate above about 0.10 mg/L increases oxygen production only a little
accept: the effect of phosphate levels off

rubric.point: A reason: another factor (such as light, nitrogen or carbon dioxide) becomes limiting once phosphate is plentiful
accept: phosphate is no longer the limiting nutrient

parts.sample: Above about 0.10 mg/L, extra phosphate raises oxygen production only a little (from 2.3 to 2.6 mg/L). This suggests phosphate is no longer the limiting factor: once algae have enough phosphate, something else, such as light or nitrogen, limits how fast they can photosynthesize.
